title: Auxiliary indices bounded by term length
statement: Let $t$ be a term on $n$ variables (a list of literals), and let $\ell$ be a list of literal–index pairs with the property that every pair in $\ell$ occurs in the indexed enumeration of $t$; that is, each entry of $\ell$ is a literal of $t$ paired with its position in $t$. Then for any decision-tree path and any restrictions $\rho_0,\sigma$, every pair $(i,b)$ appearing in the auxiliary output produced when $\ell$ is processed against the path against $t$ satisfies $i < \lvert t\rvert$.
hypotheses_covered: t is a term (list of literals) on n variables
ℓ is a list of literal-index pairs
every pair of ℓ lies in the indexed enumeration t.zipIdx
arbitrary restrictions ρ₀ and σ are given
replaced:
When the processed literals come from $t.\mathrm{zipIdx}$, every entry of the aux
output of $\mathrm{processClauseLits}$ has first coordinate strictly less than
$t.\mathrm{length}$.
